newsitem.title: UK: Gold OTC vols climb higher on sharp moves in spot.
newsitem.headline: Gold OTC vols climb higher on sharp moves in spot.

text.p: Recent sharp moves in the bullion price have sparked a surge in gold OTC option volatilities and growing interest in nearby dates, options traders said.
Gold at-the-money one-month volatilities were being bid as high as eight percent after pushing higher when spot prices tumbled last week.
Volatilities for three, six and 12 months have also edged higher, although demand was stronger for nearby dates with December and January seen as the most active.
The longer-term volatilities curve was virtually flat at around 7.3 to 7.5 percent bid, dealers said.
"There's been good interest in everything as volatility in the market has gone up," one options trader said.
"But it's impossible to say where interest is concentrated, because the way the market has been you can be $5 away from today's level in a day or two," he added.
Dealers reported interest in puts below the market, noting the $365 and $360 strike levels. But enquiries for calls for pre-Christmas dates at $371-$372 were also noted.
"In the next three months spot could go to $385 or down to $350, so there is a wide range of probability. There's been put buying and call buying depending on your view of the market."
Calls around $390-$400 were also seen for the first and second quarter of next year.
"They're cheap -- a $400 call for six months is a couple of dollars," a trader said.

Volatilities started picking up from all-time lows under four percent for one-month bids in November after the underlying price took a sharp downwards turn under heavy selling pressure and slack physical offtake.
"When we first broke below $370 (volatilities) started to move up," a dealer said.
The shake-up in spot bullion continued last Friday when spot prices moved $7 in one day on the back of a sharp losses in the equity markets.
Volumes were picking up, although most of the options interest was still coming from big players and business was sporadic ahead of the year-end holidays, dealers said.
